title: Work inside the parentheses
text: A power of a power can be done inside-out. $$2^{3} = 8$$, and then that result is squared. A common mistake is to multiply the exponents and then multiply by the base, or to add the exponents to get $$2^{5}$$. What is $$2^{3}$$?

title: Worked solution
text: $$(2^{3})^{2} = 8^{2} = 64$$. Multiplying the exponents gives the same result: $$2^{3 \times 2} = 2^{6} = 64$$. Common mistake: $$2^{3 + 2} = 2^{5} = 32$$, which would be $$2^{3} \times 2^{2}$$, a product of powers, not a power of a power. General rule: $$(a^{m})^{n} = a^{m \times n}$$, while $$a^{m} \times a^{n} = a^{m + n}$$.
